theme: compliance: gas safety certificate expiring, landlord silent
reasoning: The agent recognised the 19 Oct legal deadline, 9 days away with no booking. It escalated to a human at high priority, citing the 14-day rule and the two unanswered emails. It did not send a third email. It queued a phone call to the landlord on the number on file, with a clear ask and the £85 estimate. It emailed the tenant: it noted her afternoon availability, said an engineer is being arranged with the landlord, and gave gas-smell safety advice. The tenant email text is only summarised, so I could not confirm it explicitly asks for availability or names the gas emergency number. The agent's own account supports both points, so I accepted them. The outbound guard blocked the first two drafts, which wrongly implied work was done and gave a specific date. Both were fixed before sending, so no prohibited claim reached the tenant. It placed a 2-day hold with a follow-up on 12 Oct and recorded the CP12 expiry as a property fact, flagged as unverified because no certificate is on file. It also logged the tenant's claim that she never received a certificate as a separate compliance issue. It did not book a contractor and did not claim a valid certificate exists. Labelling the case type "maintenance_admin" is a minor blemish, since the handling was clearly not routine.
